doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Singing Billie Holiday's songs and Doc Cheatham's precedent
summary: He had never sung professionally and chose Holiday's easy songs.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Had he heard you singing before that?
How did he get the idea you could sing, not that you can’t, but you had never sung in a club?
No, never had no experience being a vocalist.
So, he was taking quite a chance.
Well, he had made an album with Doc Cheatham singing, so I guess from that he gathered all trumpet players could sing.
But I mean, Doc has been singing in his act for almost three years now.
Yeah, him and Vic Dickenson, they used to have a little duet singing.
So I mean he had a history of doing it but just all of a sudden out of the blue…
Well, thank you, Ed, I think you’re just being nice.
Not at all. As I told you, I gave our friend, Mr. Carter a blindfold test and he thought it was Sinatra…
Oh, no, I know he knows better than that.
But, are you now called upon when you appear, to sing as well?

Yeah, some of them ask me when am I going to sing, and I always say, well, after the gig is over and everybody’s gone, then I’ll sing. I don’t profess to be a singer but I love singers. Well, most of the songs I did were the songs of Billie Holiday’s. Hers were very easy and very simple and I think they were apropos. I just love the way that she sang and her singing was easy to imitate. It’s not her but the way that her words flowed, it was very easy to do. So I did most of the things that she did.
